title: Deduplicate imported private native helpers
objective: Eliminate false native import conflicts when a private checked graph and its imported helper share one authenticated declaration

oracles: the frozen PARI splitting graph compiles without duplicate helper declarations
conflicting native imports still fail closed

handoff.summary: Canonicalize imported native IR definition fingerprints so independently analyzed copies from one authenticated source are insensitive to JavaScript object-property insertion order. A natural proof-bearing direct/transitive import regression compiles and executes on all integer backends, and the 4-case PARI splitting catalog now compiles and agrees across CPython, JavaScript, GMP, and tagged backends.
risks: An initial full native run reached and passed the compiler/native-kernel coverage but failed one unrelated timing assertion under heavy parallel compilation: doubled QQ construction measured 3.677x. The isolated test immediately passed, and a complete cached rerun then passed in 364.13 seconds.

The historical Stage G/H checked-region driver assumes call facts from its original frozen monolithic baseline. The current modular baseline yields no direct-result variant even with the historical successful compiler commit; integration replay should use its passing Stage A mode rather than weakening the historical checker.
next_steps: Run the Phase0 splitting replay in Stage A mode for the current modular baseline; preserve Stage G/H as historical artifact-specific experiments.
Treat recovery of direct-result proofs for the modular imported IR as a separate optimization campaign with newly frozen evidence.
